method:
Execute original Accounts restoration and retained-API forwarding boundaries.

Synthetic cache/session/API objects are explicit inputs. The original cold
lookup executes unchanged up to provider construction; cache virtual methods
supply only their opaque input models. The desktop AP-result callback executes
unchanged up to its delegated success handler. Its later non-null-API branch
executes as a separately bounded instruction slice after product-state setup.
No authentication result, bearer token, HTTP response or wire bytes are supplied.
standardSubstitutions: Inherited standard memory/allocation/libc and uncontended mutex hooks.
explicitBoundaries: Cache lookup returns a supplied opaque stored Accounts session and nonce.
Stored-session virtual methods copy supplied username and refresh-token placeholders.
Stop before Accounts provider construction; no provider/token result is invented.
AP callback config byte1f8 is supplied0, matching the separately recovered desktop default.
The final supplied-API slice starts after product-state production with explicit registers; it does not execute that producer or the null-API alternative.
limits: No live account, credential store, profile, native process, socket or network access.
This does not claim that every original stored session selects Accounts: a separately admitted early native cache result can select Login5.
It proves retained Accounts ownership, absent cold seed and bounded non-null-API forwarding, rather than reproducing the complete original login stack.
